data.title: STOCKS | Erebor Bank’s Stablecoin Perk Backfires Into Losses
data.description:
Erebor Bank was forced to end a free stablecoin-to-cash service after professional crypto trading firms exploited the policy for arbitrage. According to Sina Finance, the losses were borne entirely by Erebor Bank.

The bank had launched the perk when it officially opened earlier this year to attract crypto customers, offering to convert stablecoins into cash at face value with no fee. According to Sina Finance, market prices for stablecoins often trade slightly below $1, creating an arbitrage opportunity for firms that buy discounted tokens and redeem them at Erebor for full value.

Wintermute and Galaxy Digital were among the firms that took part in the redemption arbitrage, according to people familiar with the matter. Erebor later notified institutions including Wintermute to stop such trades and ended the free conversion benefit for customers without large deposits.

The bank is also preparing to complete a $1.5 billion funding round at an $8 billion post-money valuation. It received a national banking charter from the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency in February, becoming the first new bank approved during U.S. President Donald Trump's second administration.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent Calls Third-Party Litigation Funding a 'Malignant Factor'
data.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent described third-party litigation funding returns as a "malignant factor" in the financial system and said the Treasury is reviewing a $5,000 check proposal. According to PANews, he said the president's intent regarding the $5,000 checks is "very real." Last week, Trump said that if Republicans win both chambers of Congress, each U.S. adult would receive $5,000.

data.title: Iranian Media Says Third U.S. MQ-1 Drone Was Intercepted and Shot Down Over Strait of Hormuz
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Iranian sources said a third U.S. MQ-1 drone was intercepted and shot down over the Strait of Hormuz by the air defense system of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Aerospace Force.

data.title: ECB Says Euro Area Households Hold €10 Trillion In Cash, Avoid Markets
data.description:
Euro area households hold nearly €10 trillion in cash and low-yield bank deposits, while around 80% own no stocks or other market investments, the European Central Bank said Tuesday. According to BeInCrypto, the ECB said the cash pile equals about a third of households’ financial assets and that more than 60% keep most wealth in property, with only 4% holding a sizeable share directly in shares, bonds or funds.

The ECB said perceived risk, weak financial literacy and low trust are the main barriers to investing, and urged faster progress on savings and investment accounts across the bloc.

data.title: AI | Noble Says AI Will Drive History’s Biggest Capital Reallocation
data.description:
George Noble, managing partner at Noble Capital Advisors and a former Fidelity fund manager, discussed artificial intelligence bear cases amid concerns over AI safety, according to Bloomberg.

The debate over how far and how fast AI is advancing has put tech executives in a difficult position as they try to reassure investors and customers after pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology.

data.title: Carlyle’s Redett Discusses Fundraising Supercycle, AI and Higher Rates
data.description:
Carlyle Co-President and Head of Global Private Equity John Redett spoke with Bloomberg’s Dani Burger from the sidelines of Carlyle’s Global Investor Conference in Washington, according to Bloomberg.

He discussed current investment opportunities, AI across the portfolio, higher-for-longer rates and private equity.

data.title: FHFA Director Bill Pulte Says Mortgage Insurers Should Allow Consumer Savings
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, FHFA Director Bill Pulte said mortgage insurers should allow consumers to save.

data.title: Judge Questions Susquehanna Insider-Trading Suit
data.description:
A federal judge dealt a setback to Susquehanna International Group’s lawsuit over alleged insider trading tied to a Chinese regulatory crackdown, denying a request to keep the traders’ accounts frozen, according to Bloomberg.

The firm said it lost tens of millions of dollars.

data.title: Phil And Penny Knight To Donate $1.1 Billion To Providence St. Vincent Medical Center
data.description: According to CNBC, Nike co-founder Phil Knight and his wife, Penny, will donate $1.1 billion to Providence St. Vincent Medical Center in Oregon and its Providence Heart Institute. The gift is one of the largest donations to a healthcare institution in American history, according to a press release, and follows the couple's $2 billion donation last year to Oregon Health & Science University's Knight Cancer Institute. The latest donation will help create Oregon's first hospital dedicated to women's health and support cardiological care at Providence's eight hospitals across the state. Providence said the money will also be used to recruit physicians, fund technological innovation and clinical trials, and support personalized patient treatment. Dr. Dan Oseran, executive medical director of the Providence Heart Institute, said the Knights' funding helped start a successful heart transplant program and allowed the hospital to recruit staff and give physicians more time for research and administrative work.

data.title: Naspers Buys Back 1.77 Million Shares for More Than 63.7 Million Euros
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, Naspers repurchased 1.771604 million shares at an average price of 35.9873 euros during the week of September 7-11, for a total of more than 63.7 million euros, equivalent to more than $74.1 million.

data.title: FAA Chief Warns Trump Air Traffic Modernization Plan Needs More Funding
data.description: According to Wallstreetcn, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford told the House Appropriations Committee that U.S. President Donald Trump's air traffic control modernization plan will be difficult to sustain unless Congress provides more funding. Bedford said the investment would otherwise lead to more flight delays, more cancellations, and more inconvenience for citizens traveling by air. The FAA has deployed 11,000 certified professional controllers and has another 4,000 in training, while a subcommittee member said those targets do not account for challenges to the current controller workforce from academy graduation rates, burnout, and early retirement.

data.title: Hayden Adams Says Robinhood Chain Is Not Dead After Fee Cut
data.description:
Uniswap founder Hayden Adams dismissed claims that Robinhood Chain is "dead," saying the conclusion based only on fee revenue charts is misleading. According to ChainCatcher, he said Robinhood simply raised the gas limit and lowered user fees to expand on-chain capacity and meet strong demand for block space.

Adams said about 95% of Robinhood Chain's DEX trading volume comes from Uniswap and that the network is still performing well. Dragonfly managing partner Haseeb previously said Robinhood Chain's on-chain revenue fell sharply after the fee cut, but DEX volume remained strong and was second only to Solana. He said the move appeared intentional, with Robinhood prioritizing lower fees and higher capacity to attract RWA and on-chain financial activity rather than maximizing short-term sequencer revenue.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Wealthy Investors Use BlackRock and Vanguard ETFs to Cut Taxes
data.description:
Large institutions are switching between nearly identical equity funds to avoid receiving dividends and the 30% tax they carry, according to Bloomberg.

The source says the strategy involves BlackRock and Vanguard ETFs.

data.title: GEOPOLITICS | Bessent to Meet Chinese Counterpart This Weekend
data.description: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said he will meet this weekend with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng ahead of a summit between US President Donald Trump and Xi Jinping later this month, according to Bloomberg.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent Says AI CEOs Can Halt Progress at Any Time
data.description: U.S. Treasury Secretary Bessent said artificial intelligence company chief executives can stop progress at any time. According to Odaily, he also said the Trump administration is at the forefront of reviewing AI models.

data.title: Cisco and Nvidia Expand Splunk Agentic AI Partnership
data.description: Cisco and Nvidia have expanded their Splunk agentic AI collaboration agreement. According to ChainCatcher, the update centers on the two companies broadening their work around Splunk's intelligent agent AI offerings.

data.title: U.S. And China Discuss Cutting Tariffs On Some Goods, Bloomberg Says
data.description:
The United States and China are discussing sharp tariff cuts on some goods, including U.S. energy and agricultural shipments, ahead of a leaders' meeting expected next week, according to Ming Pao.

Bloomberg, citing people familiar with the matter, reported that the two sides are also considering extending a one-year trade truce.

data.title: Botswana Utility Plans Fiber and Grid Fees to Nearly Triple Revenue
data.description:
Botswana’s loss-making power utility plans to charge independent producers to wheel electricity to clients over its grid and commercialize 850 kilometers (528 miles) of unused fiber, according to Bloomberg.

The measures are aimed at boosting revenue almost threefold by 2031.

data.title: Africa MDBs to Market SRTs Backing $2 Billion in Loans in March
data.description: Multilateral development banks in Africa plan to begin inviting investors to back a risk-transfer tied to $2 billion of loans early next year, according to Bloomberg.
